Study Area Selection & Coffee Agroforestry Context

Why this area was audited: Situated in Caldas Department in Colombia's Central Cordillera, this 123.21-hectare holding lies within the UNESCO-recognized Coffee Cultural Landscape of Colombia (PCCC), representative of high-altitude shade-grown Arabica cultivation (1,650–1,820m ASL).

Multi-Sensor Consensus: Combining Google FDP 10m coffee modeling (61.84% presence) with Nature Trace (49.30% natural canopy) and Forest Typology (ForTy Class 5: Agroforestry) demonstrates continuous multi-strata coffee production.

Zero Deforestation Verification: Multi-temporal analysis across Hansen GFC v1.13 and Sentinel-2 confirms 0.00 ha of forest clearance post-December 31, 2020. The standing shade canopy has remained unbroken for over two decades.

Cartographic Interpretation & Multi-Sensor Findings

Figure 1 Evidence: Cadastral-clipped optical observations verify 100% preservation of forest canopy. No red loss pixels are detected within the cadastral boundaries across the entire 2021–2025 observation window.

Figure 2 Evidence: The Google Forest Data Partnership 10m Coffee Model (`model_2026a`) maps verified coffee canopy probability reaching 77.2% across productive parcels, confirming active coffee cultivation without deforestation.

Statutory Compliance: Under EUDR Article 3(a), the absence of any post-2020 deforestation paired with verified commodity production establishes full compliance for import into the European Union.
